note: GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder cohorts consistently exhibit cerebellar atrophy and frontal hypoplasia, whereas simplified gyral pattern was reported in only a subset (e.g., 1 of 4 patients).

evidence.text: Brain imaging in four patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants demonstrated brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement and frontal lobe hypoplasia, while a simplified gyral pattern was observed in only one patient.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern.

evidence.text: Affected individuals with GTF3C3 variants frequently show cerebellar and corpus callosum malformations or cerebellar atrophy alongside frontal hypoplasia.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: cerebellar atrophy with simplified gyral pattern and hypoplastic frontal lobes bilaterally at age 15y 11m Cerebellar atrophy
